language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hello, my name is Camron. This is Loch Ness in Scotland. After school it’s my job to help take care of the lake.
Loch Ness is a habitat. A habitat is a home for living things. Plants, birds, fish, reptiles, and small mammals live here at Loch Ness.
Each creature needs the water from the lake and its surroundings to survive. They live in the Lock Ness habitat.
Today we will look for things that do not belong in the Loch Ness habitat.
Camron, don’t forget to put your tools in your backpack.
Hello, I am Tim.
Hello, my name is Camron. This is Loch Ness in Scotland. After school it’s my job to help take care of the lake.
Loch Ness is a habitat. A habitat is a home for living things. Plants, birds, fish, reptiles, and small mammals live here at Loch Ness.
Each creature needs the water from the lake and its surroundings to survive. They live in the Lock Ness habitat.
Today we will look for things that do not belong in the Loch Ness habitat.
Camron, don’t forget to put your tools in your backpack.
Debris is any rubbish that does not belong in the habitat. This can be very harmful for animals and plants. For example, animals can eat small parts of plastic and die.
Not all rubbish is equal though. Some things can be recycled: this means we can use the material again. Other things are bio-degradable.
They slowly disappear as they are eaten by micro-organisms. Other materials are non-degradable and stay around for a very long time. Can you help me clean up and put everything in the right bin?
